about: The epistola of the formulary “23rd Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: Be my imitators, and observe those who walk in this way, even as you have our example. For many walk, of whom I often told you, and now tell you even with tears, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ: whose end is perdition, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their disgrace, who set their minds on earthly things. But our way of life is in heaven, from where we also look for the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reshape the body of our low estate, conformed to the body of His radiance, according to the working by which He is able even to subject all things to Himself. Therefore, my brethren, dearly beloved and most longed for, my joy and my crown, so stand firm in the Lord, dearly beloved. I ask Evodia, and I beseech Syntyche, to think the same thing in the Lord. And I ask you also, true companion: help those women who labored with me in the Gospel, with Clement and the rest of my helpers, whose names are in the book of life.

ex.w025: The participle describes Paul himself, who writes these words in tears. Its subject is the unexpressed I of “dico” (w026), not a separate noun.
